(Today through Wednesday)...
Issued at 211 AM EST Thu Nov 12 2026

A strengthening upper level trough will expand across the eastern 
half of the country through the end of the week marking a drastic 
shift to a cooler and unsettled weather pattern. Chilly temperatures 
are expected with the chance for scattered light precipitation 
through Friday. As the upper trough moves away to the east over the 
weekend...dry weather will return with temperatures gradually 
warming through next week.

Today through Friday Night

Light rain lingers across northeast parts of central Indiana early 
this morning as low pressure tracks across southern Ohio. An initial 
surge of lower stratus in the immediate wake of the cold front was 
moving into the southeast half of the forecast area with breaks in 
the clouds further to the northwest. Northerly wind gusts were 
dropping off from speeds Tuesday evening with temps dropping quickly 
in the 40s as cold advection establishes.

The coldest air of the Fall settles over the region in the short 
term as an upper trough amplifies and then closes off an upper low 
that will drop into the eastern Great Lakes by Friday night. 
Multiple waves will pivot around the flank of the upper level trough 
maintaining plenty of low level clouds and periodic precipitation 
through Friday.

A few light showers are possible through late morning focused 
largely over the northeast half of the forecast area but subtle 
ridging aloft will briefly track through the area and largely limit 
precipitation through midday. This will also aid in delaying a 
broader stratocu deck from settling over the area until later today 
with the potential for at least some breaks in the clouds this 
morning across the southwest half of the forecast area.

The strongest of the short waves within the amplifying upper level 
trough will track across the region this afternoon. As it does so 
the wave will interact with strong cold advection and steepening mid 
level lapse rates to generate scattered to numerous light rain 
showers peaking in coverage by mid to late afternoon and focused 
particularly across the northeast half of the forecast area. The 
resumption of gusty northwest winds along with increasing stratus 
will make for a raw chilly day across the area with highs remaining 
in the 40s. 

Subtle ridging this evening will aid in decreasing shower coverage 
but yet another shortwave will pivot across the region Friday 
morning. This will maintain at least a broken stratus deck with the 
potential for renewed light precipitation that may linger into the 
day Friday. A more pronounced northerly fetch off Lake Michigan 
Thursday night into early Friday supports the development of a more 
persistent north-south band of rain and snow across northwest 
Indiana that may be able to briefly make it as far south as the 
northern Wabash Valley Friday morning before low level flow backs 
and any lingering precipitation shifts east and decreases in 
response to a weakening NW-SE flow off the lake. Model soundings do 
show a saturated airmass through about 700mb with modest lapse rates 
into Friday afternoon. This will maintain a healthy stratocu deck 
across much of the area as a result with the potential for sprinkles 
or flurries for parts of the forecast area generally to the east of 
Interstate 65. Subfreezing temps within the boundary layer also 
supports the potential for graupel to mix in at times as well. Low 
level thermals suggest 45 degrees is probably the upper bound for 
temperatures Friday afternoon.

Drier air will gradually advect into the region Friday night as 
upper level cyclonic flow relaxes resulting in a slow scattering of 
low clouds from the west as the night progresses. Lows will drop 
into the mid and upper 20s over the entire forecast area.

Saturday through the Middle of Next Week

The upper low will shift east into the Canadian Maritimes by Sunday 
with an overall transition to broad ridging aloft that will persist 
for much of next week. A scattered to broken cu field will linger 
Saturday across the northeast half of the forecast area as the upper 
low moves away. A strong high pressure ridge will pivot into the 
Ohio Valley for the second half of the weekend with a return to 
quiet weather and mainly clear skies that will last through much of 
next week. The onset of warm advection will usher in a slow warming 
trend with seasonable conditions for mid November by the middle of 
next week. Highs will largely remain in the mid and upper 40s 
through Monday...then rising into the mid and upper 50s by next 
Wednesday and Thursday. Lows will range between the mid 20s and 
lower 30s through the period.
